newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- DEC 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- DEC 16.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--A special charge on transactions will be imposed to fund the share capital of the auxiliary guarantee fund, which will operate independently of the guarantee fund, reports say. Initial share capital of the fund is projected at 1-1.5 billion drachmas, with this gradually increasing to double the average daily volume of transactions. The guarantee fund meanwhile is expected to more than double its capital to 8-10 billion drachmas.
--In a parting shot, the outgoing bourse supervisor has claimed that bourse authorities have been lax in examining reports.

--As the farmers' blockades go into their 19th day, there is hope for a solution as farmers around the country slowly dismantle barricades. Prime Minister Costas Simitis's puts the issue at the top of the agenda in his meeting today with ministers.

--The Bank of Greece has requested the government put the brake on indirect taxes, increased charges for public utilities and the state's foreign lending. In its half-yearly report, the central bank recommends the government resort to containment of public expenditure, denationalisation and domestic lending and stresses the two basic problems facing the economy: reduced competitiveness and the worsening external trade balance.

--The Capital Market will see major structural changes with the impending application of Community legislation allowing banks to be equal members of the stock exchange. The development, sources say, will lead to brokerage firms merging or seeking new cooperation with credit institutions, and the disappearance of subsidiary brokerages.
--Greek power company DEH is examining using private suppliers and producers and restructuring the domestic power supply market.

--The farmers' blockades has set off a chain-reaction in the Greek economy: In Thessaly, many units are already working below capacity and some on a reduced working week, while the first cases of profiteering have made their appearances in the increased prices for liquid gas used by factories for fuel. Transit is being burdened with added expense as trucks avoid the road blocks by ferry.
--Despite farmers' incomes increasing over the past three years, Greek farmers and cooperatives remain mired in debt.
--The finance ministry may be releasing the names of major tax evaders on the one hand, but on the other it is providing favourable terms for the self-same tax evaders.

--Financial problems has caused private airline company Venus to suspend flights following the transport ministry's decision to withdraw its operating licence. Apollo Greece has already suspending flights while a third, Air Greece, is facing serious financial problems.
